description:
TYPE: diagram
TITLE: Employment Relationships
TEXT IN IMAGE:
Employment Relationships
Employees
- Full-time
- Single employer
- Benefits
- Employment taxes are split between employee and employer

Non-employees (Contractors, Freelancers, Gig workers)
- Part-time
- Multiple employers (clients)
- No benefits
- Employment taxes must be paid entirely by employee

DATA:
- Category 1: Employees
  - Full-time
  - Single employer
  - Benefits
  - Employment taxes are split between employee and employer
- Category 2: Non-employees (Contractors, Freelancers, Gig workers)
  - Part-time
  - Multiple employers (clients)
  - No benefits
  - Employment taxes must be paid entirely by employee

KEY FACTS:
- The diagram divides employment relationships into two primary categories: Employees and Non-employees.
- Employees typically work full-time for a single employer, receive benefits, and share employment taxes with their employer.
- Non-employees include contractors, freelancers, and gig workers who often work part-time for multiple employers or clients.
- Non-employees generally do not receive benefits and must pay their employment taxes entirely by themselves.
